items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: His music is sort of like — it makes Arnold Schoenberg look like “Tea for Two” in a sense.

ctx.x: Bill Finegan, God, he’s got an interesting reputation from all his work. Further composition studies with him?

Oh yeah. Orchestration and arranging. He studied with Stephan Wolpe too. And he said Wolpe, you know a German, an emigre German basically serialist composer, extremely intense. His music is sort of like — it makes Arnold Schoenberg look like “Tea for Two” in a sense. It’s pretty — it’s really intense stuff. But very organized. But as I mentioned, Carisi studied with this guy and Eddie Sauter studied with him too. But Bill said, he had a little like downstairs room. I don’t know if that was just an apartment or…
